messages:
sylvia: Quick flag: the Classify endpoint docs show examples as an array of strings (`examples: [\"spam\", \"ham\"]`) but the OpenAPI schema expects an array of objects `examples: [{\"input\": string, \"label\": string}]`. That mismatch breaks the codegen examples and confuses users.

ana: ah thanks. which page/file?

sylvia: docs/api/classify.md around the Examples section. Someone copied an older marketing snippet.

kevin: that explains a few failing snippet-tests I saw. codegen validates examples against schema and rejects the shape. We should standardize on object form and include a short compatibility note for the simple-array editors.

matt: agreed. Proposed change: swap examples to object array, add a note and a one-line JS snippet showing how to map old arrays to objects: `examples = old.map(x => ({input: x}))`.

ana: can you also align the OpenAPI example payload and the SDK snippets (py/go)? i'll update ruby after you push.

sylvia: I'll open a PR to: 1) fix docs example, 2) update openapi/spec.yaml example, 3) update python/go snippets, and 4) add a small docs-test that asserts the page examples validate against the schema.

matt: ping me for a quick codegen run after you push. If tests fail because of naming differences, i'll coordinate with eng-platform.

deploy-bot: draft deploy preview created: https://deploy-preview-4001--docs.redwood.ai (expires in 7 days) :rocket:

kevin: small UX suggestion: in the example callout show both shapes and label one as "legacy shorthand" so people migrating see both. Then once codegen tool is patched, remove shorthand.

sylvia: noted. PR up as docs/classify-examples-object-shape. Thanks all :thumbsup:
